newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian share prices down in market lull.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian share prices down in market lull.

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell 4.16 points on Tuesday in quiet trade led by Commercial International Bank (CIB).
The Capital Market Authority all-share index slipped to 379.96 from 384.12 points on Monday while turnover was a below-average 49.84 million ($14.68 million).

"There is still a downward trend in most prices. We might be getting close to getting to the cheaper prices and the point at which investors throw their money into the market again," said Mohammed Abdullah, managing director of Intercapital.
"I expect prices to start picking up at the end of this month and the market will fly again. Now there's a chance for investors to make the most of the cheap prices," he added.
CIB lost one pound to close at 80 but it was most active share, trading in more than 5.9 million pounds.
"No one has a reason for CIB's rise," Abdullah said.
CIB's stablemate Misr International Bank/MIBANK did well, closing 10 pounds higher at 660 after shares worth more than 2.35 million pounds changed hands.
North Cairo Flour Mills was the day's second most active share, trading in more than four million pounds but it shed 5.95 pounds to close at 180.

"North Cairo has the trust of investors. They have confidence in its management and its ability to stand up to the competition of the private sector. Its high turnover is a reflection of this confidence," Abdullah said.
There was strong turnover in several other mills, but many closed either lower or unchanged. East Delta Flour Mills closed 0.5 pounds lower at 73.5 after trade in 2.86 million pounds.
Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed unchanged at 84.5 pounds after shares worth 2.36 million pounds.
Shares worth 3.57 million pounds were traded in Paints and Chemical Industries/PACHIN but the stock closed 0.39 pounds lower at 141.11.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 554.38 points from 559.91 points on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 271.82 from 274.94.
